issues.description: Element: WHERE-clause thresholds for columns einwohner_m and einwohner_w in Aufgabe 06. Problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 131-134) requires selecting Gemeinden with more than 100,000 male and more than 100,000 female inhabitants ("mehr als 100.000 männliche und mehr als 100.000 weibliche"). The reference solution (solution_repository/aufgabe06.sql lines 1-3) uses einwohner_m > 10000 AND einwohner_w > 10000 (10,000). This numeric threshold mismatch will cause student submissions that follow the textual specification to be judged incorrect against the provided solution and automated tests, and it will confuse students about the correct requirement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the threshold consistent. Preferred fix: update solution_repository/aufgabe06.sql to use the 100,000 threshold so it matches the problem text; change the WHERE clause to: WHERE einwohner_m > 100000 AND einwohner_w > 100000. Also update any automated tests to expect the 100,000 threshold. Alternatively, if 10,000 was intended, change the problem statement text to require 10,000 and document the intended threshold.

issues.description: Concept: the street/road column for Zoo entries. The problem statement refers to this column as the German word 'Straße' (with ß) in the natural-language task text, while the actual database column used in the solution is named 'strasse' (ASCII). Problem statement: 'Straße'. Solution: column identifier 'strasse'. Template file for the task is empty but students must use the exact identifier 'strasse' to pass automated checks. This difference (diacritic vs. ASCII) may confuse students who must type the exact SQL identifier and are unsure whether to use 'Straße' or 'strasse'.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier explicit in the problem statement so students can map the natural-language term to the exact column name. For example, change 'Straße' to 'strasse' or write `strasse` (e.g. 'Name, `strasse` und URL') or add a short note like 'Hinweis: im Schema heißt die Spalte `strasse` (ASCII)'.

issues.description: Concept: the area/size column used for filtering municipalities. The problem statement describes the concept as 'Fläche' (with an umlaut) in the task text, while the solution SQL uses the ASCII column name 'flaeche' in the WHERE clause. Problem statement: 'Fläche'. Solution: column identifier 'flaeche' (used in WHERE flaeche > 100). The template file is empty but students need the exact identifier 'flaeche' to write correct SQL; the diacritic vs ASCII mismatch may briefly confuse students.
issues.suggestedFix: Make naming consistent in the task text by referring to the exact database column identifier. For example, change 'Fläche' to 'flaeche' or write `flaeche` (e.g. '...mit mehr als 100 km² `flaeche` pro Landkreis') or add a clarifying note 'Hinweis: im Schema heißt die Spalte `flaeche` (ASCII)'.
